issues.title: An order to a supplier, paid with the order
issues.does: How the office buys from a supplier, the outside world's market among them: it places the order at the seller's listed price. The form pays nothing by itself: pay the whole sum into the account the seller's price list names, at the same sitting. The seller delivers once an order is paid in full, sends back money that comes with no order waiting for it, and declines an order unpaid after a week.

unit_price.description: The price of each, as the seller advertises it.

at.description: Where they are to be delivered.

account.description: The account the order is paid from.

retry_of.description: An earlier order this one repeats.

for_days.description: How many days the order may be served over.

writes.text: Order: {quantity} {kind} at {unit_price} each, delivered to {deliver_to} at {at}. Paid with this order.

routines.what: Each day the network supplies what the customers use from what the retailer holds, and more is bought from the grid when it runs below a fortnight's use. Those who ask to be supplied are taken on, and those gone taken off.
Each customer is sent a bill for the supply charge and what they used; one who has gone, their last. How often the bills go out is the order's.
